text:
marina: ACME sent an urgent note — their April invoice (INV-2024-0042) includes a large Dedicated overage for us-west2 from the weekend (2024-04-02 → 2024-04-03). They want a waiver. Snippet from the invoice: Reserved commit $16,312; Overage surge $12,120; Total $28,432. They claim the traffic should have landed on their reserved failover pool but was billed as on-demand. Dropping here to coordinate.
devin-bill: Confirmed — CS escalated. ACME ran a DR failover test and says the failover routed to on-demand instead of reserved. They're pushing for full waiver because this was a planned exercise. @sree can eng confirm routing/labels?
invoicer-bot: Invoice INV-2024-0042 generated for ACME Corp — amount $28,432 (overage line $12,120). Payment due in 30 days.
sree: Quick look at allocation logs — some allocations in us-west2 show nodepool label absent during the failover. Metering attributes to the pool tag present at allocation time. Example: "ALLOCATE pod=acme-dr labels={region:us-west2,nodepool:unlabeled}" then routed to pool=on-demand. So traffic didn't hit reserved capacity because the reservation tag wasn't applied.
sree: Sounds like config drift or an infra pipeline regression. We can add a CI gate and an infra admission check to enforce nodepool tagging. That prevents recurrence but doesn't retroactively reattribute metered usage.
carmen-cs: ACME is a long-term committed customer. They're willing to accept a compromise (not full waiver) if we pair credit with a written fix plan and SLA commitment for failovers. They're anxious to keep production predictable.
oliver-legal: Per our T&Cs, credits are for platform SLA breaches. Misrouting due to our config/automation is arguable. Legal recommends we avoid admitting liability. If Finance wants to do a goodwill credit, include a release clause: customer accepts credit as full settlement, no admission of liability. Marina — capture invoice and allocation IDs.
marina: Proposal from Finance: one-time goodwill credit of 50% of the overage ($6,060) plus an offer to waive burst charges for 2 months up to $3,000/month as a gesture (total potential concession ~ $12k). This keeps the relationship intact but avoids full precedent. Approve?
devin-bill: ACME told CS they'd accept 50% + 2mo waived bursts if we provide a written settlement and commit to the tagging guardrail in our infra. They're ready to sign that doc.
sree: Engineering can deliver a tagging enforcement change within 48 hours — add pre-deploy lint and a runtime admission check. I'll open a ticket (INFRA-4821) and include a runbook for billing attribution. We can also produce an attribution report for the disputed window to support manual adjustment.
oliver-legal: OK to proceed with the proposed goodwill credit + waiver offer. I'll draft the settlement text: one-time credit, no admission of liability, customer accepts as full settlement. CS to collect the customer's signature.
marina: I'll prepare a provisional credit memo and queue a manual adjustment pending signed settlement. Targeting to apply the credit before the next billing cycle. Finance ops will need the allocation IDs from Eng to annotate the memo.
ben: Approve one-time 50% credit + 2 months burst waiver cap. Finance to coordinate with Legal + CS. Eng to implement and confirm completion. Keep me posted if ACME pushes for more.
carmen-cs: I'll send the settlement template to ACME now and request sign-off today. Will post the signed doc here when received.
sree: Created INFRA-4821 (Tag enforcement + CI gate for reserved-nodepool assignment). Adding alerts if allocations occur without a nodepool label so ops can triage before metering.
marina: Thanks all. Leaving thread open until signed settlement and credit memos are posted. Will update invoice status once credit applied.
